reviews.title: AI readings on most “Listen” stories
reviews.text: I just ended my Apple News subscription because so many of the articles were trying to sell me something. I went instead to the New Yorker because many of the articles I read were interesting to me. Unfortunately it is a major turn-off for me  to listen to the articles read by “an automated voice” (which is the majority) and how it pronounces words wrong and has fake emotion. I don’t think I’ll be renewing at the end of the year.

reviews.title: Incredible content , clown car app
reviews.text: Please for the love of god get a new IT team and application backend. The web browser is absolutely cooked too. Why is this app so bad in 2026, stuff takes decades to load, buttons disappear, paramount + of the news apps easily. Will cancel and just read the physical edition at the local library

reviews.title: Why won’t this open????
reviews.text:
Takes so long to open (“Loading stories…”) that it is nonfunctional. I’m not talking 10 seconds, but a full minute or more. This is a magazine. What on earth are your developers doing? Quick making your MAGAZINE so bloated. 
 
Old critiques still unfixed: No other app does this. Why??? Seemingly every week I open this app and—after waiting for the app to wake up and update—click on an article only to be met with the splash screen telling me to subscribe or renew. Then once I click Log in it says “with the same accounts and yeah!!!What else would I be doing???? I’m sure there is some data-mining reason for this repeated nonsense but can someone PLEASE FIX IT. (Also your search engine is still worthless.)

reviews.title: Not loading home page
reviews.text: Recently subscribed from New Yorker directly (not via apple subscription). For two days it’s been displaying “loading today’s stories.”  Closing app does not fix the problem. Yesterday, I deleted from my Home Screen and downloaded a fresh copy of the app. This worked, but today the problem returned! Same experience on my iPhone 14.

reviews.title: Takes literally minutes to open

reviews.title: AI voices ruin experience
reviews.text: I love the magazine, but I can’t understand why the New Yorker won’t pay a human actor to do a better job than the “AI voice.” The AIs routinely mispronounce and wrongly emphasize words. It’s a bad look for the magazine and a disservice to the authors.

reviews.title: Display setting

reviews.title: Looks like they screwed it up again
reviews.text: All I ask from this app is that it picks up where I left off. This was working well for some time. Now it’s broken again. Tearing my hair out. If I stop reading for a day it takes a significant amount of time to get back to where I was.

reviews.title: Pretty terrible overall

App also keeps asking me to restore my Apple purchase, which isn’t possible because that requires internet as well. Works on wifi. Very frustrating. Possibly related to new features in iOS 26.

In iOS 27, it would not recognize my subscription. Apple support was unable to help. The problem was with Condé Nast’s sign in. Took over an hour to resolve.

reviews.title: App is awful

reviews.title: App doesn’t refresh

reviews.title: will not load new articles

reviews.title: Crosswords: Awful
reviews.text: The crossword content is obviously great but the app is so bad! No offline support! No indication in the list of puzzles when you’ve already completed one. Keyboard gets pushed partially offscreen so none of your keyboard muscle memory works.

reviews.title: No way to manage account
reviews.text: I was recently charged for a year’s subscription. I never initiated this and believe someone else did. On the website, it says I do not have an active subscription. However, the app says that I am active. There is no way for me to address this subscription on the app and when I call and email with customer service, I am told that I do not have an active account. —> somehow the the app and the desktop subscriptions are disconnected. I do not know how to successfully cancel this. It’s very frustrating. Why can’t they allow you manage your account in the app (unless they want to make it hard to end your subscription?). I am contacting the BBB and the appropriate federal agencies to bring visibility to how they are making it impossible to cancel or rectify a wrong charge.

reviews.title: Games, Search not working
reviews.text:
The App tells me to go to the Appstore and tap "update" in order to proceed. I can't find "update" anywhere on the New Yorker page. Does it work on everything except an iPad?
Update: Apparently the app store did not have the latest version, so our instruction to "update" made no sense.  An email to subscribers telling us there is a problem would have been nice and probably saved a lot of time and frustration.

reviews.title: Podcast bull***t
reviews.text: I am trying to listen to In The Dark, season 1. I can’t link it to my preferred podcast player, so I can only listen inside this app. Go try to find that season of that show on this app. A search for ‘in the dark podcast’ did not pull it up. When I did finally scratch my way thru to find the page for that show I still had to scroll down and hit next page 5 times to get to the season. Now, because of opening a different app this app stopped and I need to figure all the podcast bull***t again. If you’re not going to give me a better option thru your own app, give me access to mine.

reviews.title: So bad for so long
reviews.text: Embarrassingly dysfunctional in the year 2026/Claude era. If you get a new phone, you will lose all of your saved articles and history, even if you’re logged in with the same account. Want to search for those stories manually so you can re-save them? Good luck with the search function, which has been a travesty for years. You will surface everything but the article you’re looking for, even if you type in its exact headline or author. Like other reviewers have mentioned, you also get routinely signed out of the app.

reviews.title: Nothing works
reviews.text: Would love to rate this highly, but the app does not work.

reviews.title: Great magazine, terrible app
reviews.text: Magazine is great; app is awful. Endless cycle of trying to login on app leads to “login at newyorker.com,” asks for password …. Back to app, back to web browser.      Customer support explains they have two different apps, one for subscribers, etc. Renewal led to two subscriptions. Terrible app.

reviews.title: Another bad software update cripples app
reviews.text: Recent Condé Nast software ‘upgrade’ has eliminated the ability to download previous issues locally to one’s own device. So, you can only access the current issue of the magazine. For airline travel, you can’t have a cache of stored reading material.  Why remove this feature. Because they don’t care…

reviews.title: Lousy app for a great magazine
reviews.text: If it works, it’s great. But this app consistently fails to update content from one day to the next and then freezes, especially in games. The only way I can cure it is by logging out and then logging back in. Which is sad, because login somehow manages to be weirder and harder than any other app I use. Even Wired, another Condé Nast publication, makes login difficult, but not this difficult. E.g., telling me I’m not subscribed and not giving me any way to log in. Weird and difficult.

reviews.title: Terrible App, Constant Bugs
reviews.text: Very buggy, frustrating, hard to use app. The app frequently will not allow me to access recent issues of the magazine and constantly prompts me to subscribe even though already I have an active subscription. I it’s so bad I’m considering canceling my subscription.

reviews.title: app is not usable

reviews.title: Biased reporting
reviews.text:
What a racist bigoted antisemitic litter-box wrapper the New Yorker has become.  What a fall from its glory days of in depth, impartial journalism. I cancelled my subscription after 3 years of its historically illiterate analysis of the Middle East. The omissions and fabrications, the absence of historical perspective, the ideological vs factual reporting, leads one to wonder,
are there any adults left in the press room?  Disgraceful, and a sad illustration of how pandering to the lowest common denominator, the clamoring antizionist, has so tarnished a once respectable journal.

reviews.title: App seems to exist to frustrate.
reviews.text:
Originally, the app was just to read the print edition of the New Yorker. It worked well. Fast, reliable, and a joy. Now the app is unstable, crashes frequently, loads content I have zero interest in immediately upon opening instead of allow allowing me to access what I want to access immediately. Does not work with multiple VPNs, and each update tries to hide the magazine itself. I just want to read the print edition of the magazine on my tablet.

Each update makes this app more difficult to use.

2026 Update: continues to be sluggish; have to wait for home screen to populate items i'll never read to have the privilege to make multiple taps to my magazines; forced to re-sign in all the time. Bring back the simple, reliable, print-magazine-only app. This one is a chore. Yuck.

reviews.title: Condescending snobs
reviews.text: I learned to read in English with The New Yorker. It was magical: as someone whose mother had to quit high school at 15 to help support her family in Buenos Aires, I was gifted old issues by my English teacher. After all these years, I somehow made it to grad school in New York and became a proud subscriber. Today, I sadly realized that people like me, who come from a country like Argentina, cannot get any respect from those who write and run this magazine. If we succeed, they assume we must be cheating. If we do something with heart, they call it dirty.

reviews.title: The New Yorker deserves better
reviews.text: The NYer is a great magazine but this is a pretty subpar app. To give just one example, there is no way to search by an author name and find everything they’ve ever written for the magazine. What is the point of having such a vast digital archive (a big selling point they make everywhere) when you don’t make it super accessible and have a great search function? And why show the same suggested articles for literally everything I read? Just fix your ranking and recommendations and make some actually intuitive navigation. Overall, it functions, but I feel like anyone these days could vibe code a better experience. They need to hire a new PM/eng team.

reviews.title: A poor digital offering
reviews.text:
The New Yorker magazine is iconic. The order of the contents, familiar. The clean, text-focused design, perfection. 

The digital subscription offers a scrambled, damaged version of the magazine. The pages, out of order. Reader letters, at the end? Why? We read the magazine — we know where they should be. 

The quality of the journalism, and editing, is famous. Why, then, when I read a tuning-fork perfect final line, are my eyes assaulted by a bunch of attention seeking links to other stories? This isn't an ad-driven website; I subscribed, you have my money. Show respect for The New Yorker's format, and the people who love it.

The whole digital offering is poor, unimaginative, and dogmatically, pointlessly webified; I'd rather just have a clunky old PDF, and read my New Yorker in peace.

reviews.title: Incredibly buggy, often unusable
reviews.text: The New Yorker is a catastrophically flawed app. It is often demoralizing and humiliating to consider that I pay $200 a year for a subscription to this nearly unusable service. It is plagued with a seemingly endless onslaught of annoying bugs - most consistently, whenever you close the app, it exits the article and does not save your place so you have to then find the article again and then find your place to take up where you left off. It also decides to sign you out of your account at least twice a week and force you to go through the bureaucratic horrors of logging in again (extra fun when you are on a plane or other places without cell service). Then there are lots of exciting little bugs that whimsically appear and disappear. Most recently, every article just turned into a blank, empty endless scroll with no words after about three sentences. It might be a conflict of interest but I do think the psychology of what keeps us coming back to this awful experience would be a great subject for Jia Tolentino‘s next piece.

reviews.title: Always logging you out
reviews.text: App is constantly logging you out and forcing you to re-verify. Then it tries to get you to re-subscribe meaning there is a real chance of double or triple paying depending on whether you’re using Apple, Conde Nast or Email. Ultimately a really frustrating experience. You cannot use the app at all when you are offline. Also the reason why I’m ending my subscription despite supporting their journalism for years.

reviews.title: Cancelling a subscription
reviews.text: I love the New Yorker. I never really got to read much of it during my first few months as I was drawn into it with a story I was going to share but couldn’t find it after I had subscribed. I stuck with it for a while, 6 months or so then I began my journey to unsubscribe.  It was nearly as bad as raising a dispute with my bank for a cancelled flight due to the airline going bust but not quite. After hours of redirects and chats with 80’s type chat bots who redirected me to subscribe with a $5 off coupon , I begun to wonder if I might not just be better to continue my subscription on the grounds of sound economics. After all as it was taking me so long to leave I thought even on minimum wage I’d be better just leaving it run and sucking up the monthly cost.  It was at that point I thought I would start to write for The New Yorker as a freelancer , I could serialise my journey and in between waiting for email responses I could compare other platforms and services and how difficult they make it to leave a relationship.  I mean it couldn’t be as a hard as Divorce surely 🤔 or could it ? I was after all in the lap of the Gods the jury was still out and I was pacing up and down like an expectant Father without a cigar. Groucho Marx where are you when I need you. In the end I thought I’d adopt the persona of Harpo and 😶 try to win The New Yorker over through my music but alas I think it was all falling on deaf ears.  So I decided much like the character that couldnt leave the Airpor
